question: Can the existing frozen MotionBERT-Lite representation predict participant-level POMA-Gait and TUG in previously unseen Toronto participants?
source: Toronto Older Adults Gait Archive: PoseTracking.zip and Table 1.xlsx
pose_method: Alphapose only, selected from the prior structural audit before score prediction

selection.required_header: time plus 17 COCO x/y/conf triples; reject absent columns
selection.valid_source_row: all values finite, all confidence in [0,1], six lower-body joints have confidence > 0
selection.continuous_time: positive adjacent timestamps, gap <= 1.5 times the median positive source interval
selection.window: first 4.1 seconds of longest valid continuous time span; ties use earliest span; exactly one window per CSV
selection.resampling: linear x/y/conf interpolation at 30 Hz between observed adjacent valid rows only; no crossing missing rows or dropped-frame gaps; no extrapolation or padding

analysis_unit: one participant; average their eligible window feature vectors with equal window weights
target_handling: separate continuous regressions; original values, no rounding, clipping, thresholding or combined score
outer_evaluation: leave one participant out; every eligible participant evaluated exactly once

PLS.selection: inner leave-one-training-participant-out MAE for each target; smallest component count breaks ties; never use outer participant

standardization: StandardScaler fitted only on the relevant training participants; refitted for each inner and outer split
constant_training_target: predict training mean instead of fitting PLS
metrics: paired absolute-error difference from training-median baseline

uncertainty.interpretation: exploratory intervals conditional on these OOF predictions, not an independent clinical validation

interpretation: Compare with both constant baselines; report individual errors and target imbalance. No clinical success threshold is introduced and no best method is adopted using this outer evaluation.
